results.title: H100 SXM Deep Dive: Pricing Across 19 Marketplaces — Week of August 31 - September 6, 2026 | AIMC | AIMC
highlights:
The H100 SXM median rental rate rose 1.2% week-over-week, moving from $3.25 to $3.29 per GPU-hour, according to AIMC observations. That narrow headline move obscures meaningful dispersion across individual marketplaces: the spread between the lowest and highest observed ask prices this week spans more than $0.80 per GPU-hour, a gap that carries material implications for operators sourcing at scale. The analysis that follows breaks down H100 SXM pricing marketplace by marketplace, documents the specific rate each venue is posting, and quantifies how far each sits from the $3.29 median. The data covers the seven-day window ending this reporting period and reflects listed rates as observed, without normalization for contract length or reserved versus on-demand tier distinctions.

## This Week in Numbers

- Focus SKU: H100 SXM
- Week-over-week move: +1.2% ($3.25 → $3.29 median across covered marketplaces)
- Marketplace coverage: 19 marketplaces, 322 observations this week
- Price range: $1.89/hr at upcloud to $10.00/hr at huggingface

Across the 19 marketplaces carrying H100 SXM this week, the observed median ranged from $1.89/hr at upcloud to $10.00/hr at huggingface — a 5.3x spread between the lowest and highest median. Intra-SKU spreads of this magnitude reflect differences in commitment terms, regional availability, and how aggressively each provider is positioning the same hardware, rather than differences in the silicon itself. AIMC reports each marketplace's observed median independently and does not blend them into a single figure that would mask this dispersion — the spread itself is part of what the market is telling you.

...

The most striking feature of this week's H100 SXM data is not the direction of its median price movement but the extraordinary width of the pricing landscape surrounding it. Ai Mining Co. tracked 19 active marketplaces offering H100 SXM capacity this week, and the spread between the lowest and highest observed median hourly rates ran from $1.89 on Upcloud to $10.00 on Hugging Face — a 5.3x differential across what is nominally the same compute unit. A spread of this width suggests that buyers are not encountering a unified market for this SKU; they are encountering a collection of distinct market segments that happen to share a hardware label. Differences of this magnitude are broadly consistent with variation in commitment structures, with some platforms pricing short-burst or on-demand access at a substantial premium relative to providers whose rates may reflect longer reservation terms or regional supply conditions — though the data alone cannot confirm which variable is driving any individual platform's position on that range.

results.title: Cheapest GPU cloud: Comparing AI compute rental prices
highlights:
While GPU clouds advertise low hourly rates, true costs vary wildly based on billing increments, egress fees, and storage. This guide provides a framework to normalise quoted prices and compare AI compute rental offers on equal terms.

...

Key takeaways

- An hourly rate is only comparable when normalised for GPU memory, interconnect, billing granularity and commitment term.
- Cost components like storage, data egress, and idle time sit outside the nominal hourly rate and alter the final price.
- Lambda charges 3.99 USD per hour for a 1x H100 SXM with no egress fees, while AWS offers a p5.4xlarge H100 at 5.191 USD.
- Publicly funded EU capacity like the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking offers an alternative 8.2 billion EUR access model.

...

This guide sets out how to normalise GPU rental prices that are quoted on different bases, so two offers can actually be compared. Headline hourly rates published on cloud provider storefronts rarely represent the complete invoice cost of executing an AI workload. A quoted rate of 3.00 USD per accelerator hour can easily result in higher total expenditure than a 4.50 USD offer once interconnect bandwidth, storage allocations, network egress fees, and minimum billing durations are factored into the calculation.

...

Cloud pricing structures fall into three primary commitment tiers: spot/interruptible instances, on-demand instances, and reserved capacity blocks. Spot instances offer discounts of 40% to 70% below on-demand rates but can be reclaimed by the provider with minimal notice, making them unsuitable for latency-sensitive production services without automated checkpoint recovery. On-demand instances offer guaranteed execution for ad-hoc jobs, while capacity blocks allow teams to reserve GPU nodes for fixed time windows without multi-year commitments. Independent benchmarking platforms such as Artificial Analysis [1] emphasize that measuring effective infrastructure cost requires tracking output throughput alongside raw compute expenses.

...

The nominal compute rate is only one component of a cloud bill. In enterprise deployments, auxiliary infrastructure charges often add 15% to 40% to the base compute cost. For short-lived jobs, data-intensive pipelines, or bursty fine-tuning runs, secondary billing mechanisms frequently exceed the initial price differential between competing providers.

...

| Cost Parameter | Lambda 1x H100 SXM (On-Demand) | AWS EC2 Capacity Block p5.4xlarge (1x H100) | Variance / Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Nominal Hourly Rate | 4.29 USD / hr | 5.191 USD / hr | AWS base rate is 21.0% higher |
| 4-Hour Compute Charge | 17.16 USD | 20.76 USD | 4.29 USD x 4 vs 5.191 USD x 4 |
| Storage Allocation (500 GB) | Included (2.75 TiB SSD base) | ~0.13 USD (EBS gp3 pro-rated) | Attached block storage |
| Outbound Data Egress (30 GB) | 0.00 USD (No egress fees) | ~2.70 USD (at 0.09 USD / GB) | Internet egress charge |
| Total Effective Invoice | 17.16 USD | 23.59 USD | Effective variance reaches 37.5% |

...

In this comparison, both options provide access to a single NVIDIA H100 80GB GPU. Lambda lists a single on-demand H100 SXM instance at 4.29 USD per hour, configured with 26 vCPUs, 225 GiB of system RAM, and 2.75 TiB of local SSD storage [3]. AWS provides its 1x H100 capacity via the EC2 p5.4xlarge instance type through EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML, priced at an effective hourly reservation rate of 5.191 USD in US East regions.

...

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| Google Cloud | Accelerator-optimized A3/A4 | H100 / B200 GPUs | Custom / On-demand | Per-second | Billed separately | September 2026 |

### Hyperscaler reservation models versus GPU-native clouds

Hyperscalers offer high infrastructure reliability and broad enterprise compliance frameworks, but their pricing structures reflect substantial overhead. AWS EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML provide predictable access to clusters like the p5.48xlarge (8x H100) at 37.76 USD per hour in London and Stockholm (4.720 USD per accelerator hour) and 41.528 USD per hour in US East (5.191 USD per accelerator hour). In contrast, specialised GPU providers such as Lambda list 8x H100 SXM nodes at 31.92 USD per hour (3.99 USD per accelerator hour) [3], and RunPod offers individual H100 PCIe instances on Secure Cloud starting from 2.89 USD per hour [4]. Standard knowledge-base reference sets note that pricing parity varies significantly across node architectures.

...

However, marketplace pricing reflects dynamic auction models ... Hardware reliability, host uptime, network throughput, and data isolation vary considerably between hosts.

...

Rental prices for a single NVIDIA H100 GPU vary widely based on the provider and commitment. For example, Lambda charges 3.99 USD per hour for an H100 SXM instance with no egress fees, while AWS offers a p5.4xlarge H100 via Capacity Blocks at 5.191 USD per hour.

results.title: AWS GPU Price Increases 2026: What to Do About It
highlights:
EC2 Capacity Blocks went up around 15% in January and again in July. The increases track the memory shortage, and they change which GPU cloud is actually cheapest for your workload.

## Key takeaways

- AWS raised EC2 Capacity Block prices for ML twice in 2026, and as of October 2026 P6-B300 lists at $16.146 per accelerator-hour in us-east-1.
- Measure utilization per block before renewing, move portable training jobs to cheaper GPU clouds, and keep latency-sensitive inference where your data already lives.

...

AWS raised EC2 Capacity Block prices for ML in January and again on 1 July 2026, so re-run your GPU budget now. Measure utilization per block, split training from inference, price the portable training half at specialist clouds, and renew only blocks you keep above roughly 70% busy. Production inference inside AWS usually stays put.

...

## The rates as of October 2026

These are the per-accelerator-hour Capacity Block rates on AWS's pricing page at the end of October 2026. Every instance has 8 accelerators, so multiply by 8 for the instance-hour.

| Instance | Accelerator | Region shown | Per accelerator-hour | Per instance-hour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P6-B300 | 8 x B300 | US East (N. Virginia) | $16.146 | $129.17 |
| P6-B200 | 8 x B200 | US East (N. Virginia) | $14.208 | $113.66 |
| P5en | 8 x H200 | US East (N. Virginia) | $7.895 | $63.16 |
| P5e | 8 x H200 | US East (Ohio) | $6.866 | $54.93 |
| P5 | 8 x H100 | US East (N. Virginia) | $5.970 | $47.76 |
| P4de | 8 x A100 | US East (N. Virginia) | $2.546 | $20.37 |

When we first wrote this in September, P6-B300 was about $14.04 and P6-B200 about $12.355, so the published rates have moved up roughly another 15% since. The page says prices are updated regularly based on supply and demand, that the next scheduled update is January 2027, and that you pay the rate in effect when you buy, even if the block starts after an update. That last point is the one to act on: if you know you need a block in Q1, buying it before January locks today's rate.

...

As far as we can tell, the increases are not a pricing experiment. They track the same component shortage that is repricing ordinary server memory, and accelerators are the sharp end of it. High-bandwidth memory sits on the accelerator package, and HBM is exactly what memory manufacturers have been redirecting fab capacity toward because it earns multiples of what conventional DDR5 earns. The result is that the scarce input is not the GPU die. It is the memory stacked next to it.

...

The practical effect of two increases in one year is that the spread between AWS and the specialist GPU clouds widened. Hourly rates for the same class of accelerator already varied widely across providers before this year, and the gap moved in the specialists' favour. We keep the detailed numbers in the GPU cloud comparison.

...

If you hold Capacity Blocks that renew in the next two quarters, the sequence that works is: measure real utilization per block, split the workload into training and inference, price the training half at two specialist providers, and only then decide what to renew.

results.title: Nvidia's 3-Year-Old H100 Chip Is Still Getting the Market to Pay Up, Jensen Huang Says Compute Is 'Fungib - Benzinga
highlights:
On Monday, Nvidia Corp (NASDAQ: NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang doubled down on his view that AI computing hardware is becoming a valuable, financeable asset as rental prices for the company’s older H100 GPUs continue to climb.

## Huang Calls Nvidia Compute a ‘Revenue-Generating Asset’

"NVIDIA compute is fungible, durable and highly rentable," Huang wrote in a post on X. "It is a productive, revenue-generating asset."

His comments came in response to Ornn Exchange, which said its Compute Price Index showed the rental price for Nvidia’s three-year-old H100 had climbed 22% in a month to $3.28 per hour.

The increase is notable because conventional depreciation models generally assume that older hardware loses value over time. Strong demand for AI computing, however, is helping some Nvidia GPUs maintain or even increase their rental economics.

...

If GPUs can consistently generate revenue through rentals, investors and lenders can potentially assess them more like productive infrastructure than conventional depreciating equipment.

results.title: 英伟达 H100、B200 租金月涨超 10% | AI头条
highlights:
# 英伟达多款 GPU 的算力租赁价格正在回升，其中 H100、B200 近一个月涨幅均超过 10%，RTX 5090 涨幅接近 30%。

算力市场数据提供商 Ornn 公布的最新数据显示，截至 2026 年 9 月 5 日，英伟达 B200 租赁价格为每块 GPU 每小时 6.42 美元，近 7 天上涨 6.0%，近 30 天上涨 11.7%。

H100 SXM 租赁价格升至每小时 3.06 美元，近 7 天上涨 6.8%，近 30 天上涨 12.7%。

A100 SXM4 报每小时 1.09 美元，近 7 天和近 30 天分别上涨 5.5% 和 4.4%。

消费级旗舰显卡 RTX 5090 的租赁价格涨幅最高，目前为每小时 0.63 美元，近 7 天上涨 18.0%，近 30 天上涨 27.6%。

H200 的走势有所不同。其最新租赁价格为每小时 4.55 美元，近 7 天上涨 2.6%，但近 30 天仍下跌 7.5%。

Ornn Compute Price Index（OCPI）依据新型云服务商市场的实际成交数据编制，采用成交量加权并进行极值处理，每个交易日结算一次。该指数反映的是 GPU 按需租赁市场价格，不包括预留算力、长期租赁合同和远期合约，也不代表英伟达调整 GPU 硬件售价。

从具体走势看，H100 和 B200 等数据中心 GPU 的租金重新走高，反映训练、推理等 AI 工作负载对高端算力的需求仍在吸收新增供给。

不过，不同型号之间已经出现分化，H100、B200 和 RTX 5090 月内上涨，H200 则尚未收复此前跌幅。

results.title: 算力岛弹性资源与青椒云科研服务器：灵活租赁方案怎么挑？
highlights:
2026年，算力需求已成为支撑技术创新的底层基础设施。中国信通院数据显示，2026年一季度国内算力租赁市场规模已达680亿元，同比增长62%，全年预计将达到2600亿元。在AI大模型训练、科学计算、数字孪生等应用持续走强的背景下，高端GPU的出租率超过90%，市场整体呈现供不应求的态势。与此同时，全球高端GPU受出口管制影响进口量受限，租赁价格上修超过40%，H100租赁价格已飙升至每小时每块GPU约2.35美元。

...

在定价方面，Lambda Labs的H100 80GB按需价格约为每小时2.49美元，A100 80GB约为每小时1.29美元，H200约为每小时3.49美元。最小计费时长为1小时，支持多节点集群（8卡），配备持久存储（NFS），并提供完整的CLI和API管理接口。其定价方式在专业GPU云服务商中属于较为透明的一类，同时支持预留实例模式，对于需要长期、稳定使用的用户，可通过预留实例获得一定比例的价格折扣。

...

当前算力租赁市场的主流计费模式主要分为按需弹性派和长期包月派两类。按需弹性派以小时或分钟为计费颗粒度，单价相对较高（约2.2-2.7元/小时），但支持随时启停，适合任务负载波动较大的场景。长期包月派则通过包月或包年锁定较低单价（约1.5-1.8元/小时），但需承诺一定的使用时长。

 一个较为实用的判断标准是：若单台服务器日均使用时长超过8小时且使用周期超过3个月，长期包月或预留实例模式通常更有成本优势；若任务负载波动较大、仅为阶段性使用（如每月仅使用10天以内），按需租赁或按量计费模式则更为灵活。对于高校课题组而言，可以考虑“核心训练节点长期持有+边缘算力按需扩展”的组合策略，在平衡成本和弹性的同时保证核心任务不中断。

results.title: Mysteel日报：高端训练卡价格持稳，H200现货集群集中放量_我的钢铁网
highlights:
9月7日，国内GPU算力租赁市场整体偏强运行，英伟达系列GPU租赁价格传出多数涨价消息，从供需终端维度进一步验证全球算力紧缺格局。消费级卡价格涨跌互现，高端训练卡价格维持高位，市场交投活跃度显著提升。

长三角区域，RTX 4090 24G单卡按需报收2.00元/卡·时，较前日上涨2.04%；RTX 4090 24G单卡包月报收1.81元/卡·时，环比上涨4.02%。整机方面， A10 24G整机包月报7.89元/卡·时，环比下降1.99%。市场整体平稳。

京津冀区域，所有型号价格与上周末持平。RTX 4090 24G单卡按需报2.11元/卡·时，环比涨0.96%、单卡包月报1.84元/卡·时，环比涨3.37%，A10 24G整机包月6.91元/卡·时，环比跌2.12%，其余型号与上日持平，市场交投稳定。

成渝方面价格亦整体小幅回落，RTX 5090 32单卡包月报2.01元/卡·时，环比下降6.07%，4090 48G单卡包月报1.92元/卡·时，环比微有上浮。而西部RTX 4090 24G单卡按需报1.89元/卡·时，同样略有上调。

高端训练卡方面，H100、H200、H800等主力机型价格维持不变，价格中枢依旧高位，高端算力紧供给格局未发生实质性改变。

...

本日H200现货租赁持续火热。新疆128台现货资源集中报出，五年闭口月租12.5万元/台，高配置，已点亮，IB组网，押一付一，不接受多层居间。H200当前资源紧缺正在向前端市场传导，卖方定价权增强。

超威B300 3T 128台期货持续报盘，价格1130万元/台，包含居间费由买方出，限价1150万元/台，交货周期4-8周（免责2周），深圳交货，卖方主体为国企。付款方式为甲方预付50%，乙方先银行开履约保函55%，见索即付。居间等比例前置，通用罚则5%，转卖罚则10%。B300顶配现货报价持续高位，优质算力进入抢货模式。

H800现货一台，浙江机房，配置HGX H800 80GB×8，一年闭口，押一付一，价格7.4万元/月。另有H20 96G整机一台，环京资源，配置Intel Sapphire Rapids 8457C×2、64GB DDR5-4800×32，含配套机柜价格4万元/月，带宽15元/M，测试机及机器交期均为随时，一年闭口，付一押一。

...

展望本周，国内GPU算力租赁市场呈现以下特征：

消费级卡方面，RTX 5090和RTX 4090等品种价格整体持稳，4090价格在长三角及京津冀区域有所上行。5090整机系统批量资源快速消化，消费级卡集群化租赁需求持续旺盛。中小客户推理需求提供底部支撑，预计以窄幅震荡为主。

高端训练卡方面，H200现货资源或有放量。西北128台等多批次资源集中入市，报价区间持续在12万元/台·月以上，闭口时间较长，卖方定价权明显增强。B300期货报价持续活跃，英伟达系列GPU租赁价格多数上涨，高端算力紧供给基本面未改。

综合判断，本轮算力需求周期较长，高端AI芯片、先进封装及高速互联等关键环节仍存供给瓶颈，技术扩散和产能释放相对较慢，预计短期算力租赁市场以高位震荡为主，需重点关注B300期货定价变化、H200供需变化对价格的影响、以及国际AI算力价格对国内市场的传导效应。
